cohort: The study included 140 antenatal patients from Kozhikode, Kerala, divided into 70 cases with threatened miscarriage and 70 controls.
finding: Threatened miscarriage was significantly associated with increased risks of preterm labor, preterm premature rupture of membranes, caesarean section, fetal growth restriction, and low birth weight.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was significantly higher in patients with threatened miscarriage (66.2%) compared to controls (42.9%).
